name: UnSub (multi-agent AI framework vs. Taiwan government) — Dream Security
akas: "Chinese-language operator" per linguistic analysis only (Simplified/Traditional Chinese code-switching); no confirmed nation-state or named APT/UNC attribution
brief: Dream Security recovered a ~160MB/1,395-file operational workspace revealing a multi-agent AI framework built on the open-source Hermes (Nous Research) and "OpenClaw" agent frameworks, running up to 8 concurrent sub-agents, a documented Bayesian two-layer probabilistic decision engine for exploit-chain scoring, autonomous "Learning Cycles" (v1–v5) pulling CVEs/PoCs from GitHub, multi-agent self-correction that removed 7 false positives, and Tesseract OCR for CAPTCHA solving — across 12 attack waves in a government-portal → nuclear-safety-agency → energy-sector targeting chain. Dream Security's own post withholds the victim country; Financial Times first named Taiwan, independently corroborated by The Register, CNN, Taipei Times, Dark Reading, CyberScoop, and others. Dream Security
